# CLARO

> CLARO (Constrained Linear Allocation and Resource Optimiser) is free, open-source
> decision-support software that allocates a fixed marketing budget across advertising
> platforms and business objectives using linear programming. It turns historical KPI
> performance, business priorities and real operating constraints into a single auditable
> optimisation model, then explains which constraints shaped the result.

- Author: Hoda Rezvanjoo (ORCID 0009-0006-3882-2669)
- Licence: MIT — free for commercial use
- Version: 0.2.1
- Solver: linear programming via PuLP with the CBC backend
- Language: Python >=3.10
- Install: `pip install claro-engine`

## What it does

Given a fixed budget, a set of marketing objectives (awareness, engagement, website
traffic, lead generation) and historical platform performance, CLARO solves a linear
program over platform-objective cells. It maximises weighted KPI productivity subject to
explicitly declared constraints: total budget, per-platform minimum spend, per-objective
minimums, a test-and-learn reserve, seasonality multipliers, and diminishing-returns
brackets that stop any single cell absorbing the plan. It then reports binding
constraints and shadow prices so the result can be interrogated rather than trusted.

Twelve advertising platforms are supported with CSV import: Facebook, Instagram,
LinkedIn, YouTube, Google Search, Google Display, Google Performance Max, TikTok,
Pinterest, X (Twitter), Snapchat and Reddit.

## What it does not do

CLARO does not operate campaigns, place bids or connect to advertising platform APIs, and
it does not estimate causal incrementality. It works from CSV exports and inherits the
strengths and biases of the KPI data supplied.

## Who it is for

Marketing and media planners, analytics and marketing science teams, agencies and
consultants, and researchers or students studying applied operations research.
